family.name: Jeep
family.verdict: The Jeep is the boxy 4x4 everyone else gets compared to, even the ones that got there first. It leaks, rattles and rusts, and it keeps selling, mostly to people who have already owned three.
intro: The civilian Jeep began with the CJ-2A of 1945, and the CJ (Civilian Jeep) line reached the [[jeep/cj-5|CJ-5]] for the 1955 model year, after Kaiser had bought Willys. It was based on the Korean War-era M38A1, and 603,303 were built before it ended in 1983. American Motors bought Kaiser Jeep in 1970 and gave the CJ its own straight-six and V8 engines from 1972. In 1976 AMC stretched the wheelbase to make the [[jeep/cj-7|CJ-7]], which became the definitive square-door CJ.

The CJ-7 and the long-wheelbase [[jeep/cj-8|CJ-8 Scrambler]] gave way in 1986 to the [[jeep/yj|Wrangler YJ]], which AMC had designed to be more comfortable on the road. The Wrangler then moved to coil springs with the [[jeep/tj|TJ]] and its long-wheelbase [[jeep/tj-unlimited|Unlimited (LJ)]], to four doors with the [[jeep/jk-unlimited|JK Unlimited]], and on to today's [[jeep/jl|JL]] and [[jeep/jl-unlimited|JL Unlimited]], which is also offered as the 4xe plug-in hybrid and the V8 392.

The boxy Jeeps weren't all open-topped. The full-size Wagoneer of 1963 became the [[jeep/grand-wagoneer|Grand Wagoneer]], a wood-sided V8 wagon built until 1991. In 1984 the unibody [[jeep/cherokee-xj|Cherokee XJ]] arrived, and from 1987 it carried the 4.0-liter version of AMC's straight six. Both have their own pages here, as does every Wrangler. Their old rivals are here too: the [[land-cruiser/fj40|FJ40]] and the [[land-rover/series|Series Land Rover]].

generations.name: CJ-5
generations.summary: Derived from the M38A1 military Jeep. Rounded door cutouts, Kaiser then AMC power, and 603,303 built across 29 years.

generations.name: CJ-7
generations.summary: The CJ-5's 10-inch-longer, square-door evolution: room for an automatic, optional hardtop and steel doors, and AMC's 258 six. Nearly 380,000 were built.

generations.name: CJ-8 Scrambler
generations.summary: A CJ-7 stretched to a 103.5-inch wheelbase, with a removable half cab and a small pickup bed. Ronald Reagan kept one at his ranch.

generations.name: Wagoneer & Cherokee (SJ)
generations.summary: The original 1963 Wagoneer and its 1974 two-door Cherokee spin-off: Quadra-Trac, AMC sixes and V8s up to the 401, and the wide-track Chief.

generations.name: Grand Wagoneer (SJ)
generations.summary: The full-size SJ wagon that began as the 1963 Wagoneer, renamed Grand Wagoneer for its final luxury-V8 years.

generations.name: Cherokee XJ
generations.summary: The compact unibody Cherokee, with the 4.0-liter straight six from 1987. It was the template for the modern SUV.

generations.name: Comanche MJ
generations.summary: The Cherokee XJ turned into a compact pickup: XJ unibody up front, a fully boxed frame behind the cab, two bed lengths and the 4.0 six from 1987. 190,446 were built.

generations.name: Wrangler YJ
generations.summary: The first Wrangler, with square headlights and leaf springs. Track bars and anti-roll bars made it more civil than the CJ.

generations.name: Grand Cherokee ZJ
generations.summary: The first Grand Cherokee: coil-sprung solid axles, a 4.0 six or Magnum V8, Quadra-Trac and the one-year 5.9 Limited. Now one of the cheapest coil-sprung solid-axle 4x4s to buy.

generations.name: Wrangler TJ
generations.summary: Coil springs and round headlights return on the short wheelbase. Many people think it's the best-riding classic Wrangler.

generations.name: Wrangler Unlimited (LJ)
generations.summary: The long-wheelbase TJ: more cargo room, a calmer ride and a short production run.

generations.name: Wrangler JK (2-door)
generations.summary: A bigger, wider and more refined two-door Wrangler. In the US it had V6 power: a 3.8 at first, then the 3.6-liter Pentastar from 2012.

generations.name: Wrangler JK Unlimited (4-door)
generations.summary: The first four-door Wrangler, and the one that took Jeep from niche toy to family car.

generations.name: Wrangler JL (2-door)
generations.summary: The current two-door Wrangler, more modern inside and out, refreshed for 2024.

generations.name: Wrangler JL Unlimited (4-door)
generations.summary: The four-door JL, including the 4xe plug-in hybrid and the V8 Rubicon 392.

generations.name: Gladiator JT
generations.summary: A JL Unlimited with a 137.3-inch wheelbase and a five-foot bed: Jeep's first pickup since the Comanche, with a 3.6 V6 or, for 2021–23, the 3.0 EcoDiesel. Refreshed for 2024.

forums.name: JeepCJ.com Community — CJ7
forums.note: The busiest CJ-only board, with CJ-5, CJ-7 and CJ-8 subforums and a buyer's-guide wiki.

forums.name: WAYALIFE Jeep Forum
forums.note: A large all-Jeep forum, strong on Wrangler builds, with plenty of CJ restorations too.

forums.name: International Full Size Jeep Association (IFSJA)
forums.note: The home of SJ Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer and J-truck owners.

forums.name: NAXJA (North American XJ Association)
forums.note: The Cherokee XJ club and forum: unibody repair, 4.0 tech and trail runs.

forums.name: WranglerTJForum
forums.note: TJ and LJ owners' forum. Its tire-fitment threads come up in most searches.

page.title: Jeep CJ-7
page.verdict: The CJ-7 is the classic Jeep that still makes sense: a longer wheelbase, real doors, AMC's unkillable 258 six and a gear-driven transfer case. It's also a 40-year-old steel tub on a frame that cracks by the steering box, so bring a magnet and a hammer when you go to look at one.

paragraphs: American Motors bought Kaiser Jeep in 1970 (for $70 million by Wikipedia's account; Jeep's own history says about $75 million), and in 1976 it gave the little [[jeep/cj-5|CJ-5]] a bigger brother. The CJ-7 sat on a 93.5-inch wheelbase, ten inches longer than the CJ-5's, and Jeep says the extra length was there to make room for an automatic transmission. The side openings were squared off to take doors, and for the first time a Jeep CJ could be ordered with a molded plastic hardtop and steel doors. It ran for eleven model years, and Wikipedia counts 379,299 built.

story.heading: THE AMC RECIPE
paragraphs: Under the tub, the CJ-7 has two parallel C-section frame rails, stepped outward at the rear so the springs and shocks sit closer to the body, with leaf springs at both ends. The front axle is an open-knuckle Dana 30. At the back is AMC's own Model 20, which has a big 8⅞-inch ring gear but thin 29-spline shafts, each made of two pieces: a hub keyed and nutted onto the shaft. Wheels use the old CJ bolt pattern of 5 on 5.5 inches.

The engines came from AMC. Early trucks had the 232 straight six as standard, with the 258 optional until it became the base six for 1979. The 258 is the one owners talk about: cast iron, seven main bearings, hydraulic lifters and enough low-end torque to idle up a hill. Offroaders.com lists it at 110 hp and 195 lb-ft in 1979–81, then 115 hp and 210 lb-ft from 1982 with a computer-controlled Carter BBD two-barrel. The 304 V8 was offered until 1981, choked by smog equipment to 125 hp by the end. From 1980 a GM 151 'Iron Duke' four was standard, rated at 82 hp. JeepCJ.com's buyer's guide tells you to skip it.

story.heading: GEARBOXES, TRANSFER CASES AND QUADRA-TRAC
paragraphs: Early trucks (1976–79) got a three-speed T-150 or the Borg-Warner T-18. From 1977 the T-18A had a 6.32:1 granny first, and Offroaders.com calls it the best transmission the factory ever put in a CJ. Behind it was a Dana 20 with a feeble 2.03:1 low range. The alternative was Quadra-Trac, a Borg-Warner 13-39 chain-drive full-time system bolted to a TH400 automatic. It had a vacuum-operated 'Emergency Drive' lock and an optional bolt-on low-range unit (2.57:1). Jeep had introduced Quadra-Trac on its full-size trucks in the early 1970s (the 1973 model year, by Wikipedia's dating), years before the [[jeep/grand-wagoneer|Grand Wagoneer]] name existed.

For 1980 everything changed. The Dana 300 arrived with a 2.62:1 low range, and Novak Conversions calls it the 'gold standard' of transfer cases. It came with lighter Borg-Warner gearboxes: the SR-4 in 1980–81, then the T-4 and five-speed T-5 from 1982. Novak's verdict on those is 'essentially a small car transmission in a truck'. The tougher choice was the Tremec T-176 four-speed (1980–86), and a Chrysler TF999 three-speed automatic replaced the TH400.

story.heading: WIDE TRACK, GOLDEN EAGLES AND LAREDOS
paragraphs: In 1982 the axles grew. The narrow-track AMC 20 measured 50.5 inches wheel to wheel, and the wide-track version 54.5 inches, which made the CJ-7 noticeably more stable. AMC also understood showroom bait. The Renegade ran the whole production life. The Golden Eagle (on the CJ-7 from 1977 to 1980, tied to the 304 V8 per Wikipedia) added a tachometer, a clock and the big Golden Eagle decals; a white 1980 CJ-7 Golden Eagle named 'Dixie' became famous as Daisy Duke's Jeep on The Dukes of Hazzard. The Laredo (1980–86) brought high-back leather seats, a tilt wheel and a chrome package.

The collectible ones are the Limited, built in 1982–83 (2,500 of them), and the 1982 Jamboree. That was 630 numbered CJ-7s, each with the 4.2-liter six, built for the 30th anniversary of the Rubicon Trail.

story.heading: LAST OF A GREAT BREED
paragraphs: The CJ's reputation took a hit in December 1980, when 60 Minutes aired an IIHS rollover demonstration of a CJ-5. AMC green-lit a replacement in 1982, and the [[jeep/yj|Wrangler YJ]] was designed to be more comfortable on the road and harder to flip, with track bars and anti-roll bars. It was unveiled in February 1986 and went on sale on 13 May 1986. The last CJ-7s carried a dash plaque that read 'Last of a Great Breed', and by then AMC 20 supplies had run so low that some 1986 trucks left the factory with wide-track Dana 44 rear axles.

The CJ-7 has outlived its replacement's reputation. AMC was working with Renault by the end, and Chrysler took over Jeep in 1987. The [[jeep/cj-8|CJ-8 Scrambler]], the YJ and the [[jeep/tj|TJ]] all owe it something. Against its 1970s rivals, the [[land-cruiser/fj40|FJ40]] and the [[land-rover/series|Series Land Rover]], the CJ-7's case in the US was cheap parts, easy modification and a huge aftermarket, and that case still holds: almost every part is still reproduced.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE CJ-7 AMERICA NEVER GOT
callout.title: Isuzu diesels and Canadian Army Jeeps
paragraphs: From 1980 to 1982 AMC built an export-only CJ-7 diesel in Ohio. It had Isuzu's 2.4-liter C240 four, a T-176 gearbox, a Dana 300 (Wikipedia says some reportedly got a Dana 20) and, typically, narrow-track axles with 4.10 gears.

In 1985 the Canadian Army took delivery of 195 militarized CJ-7s, codified as Equipment Configuration Code 121526. They were a stop-gap between the retirement of the M38A1 and the arrival of the Bombardier Iltis, so the CJ, born of a military Jeep, ended up back in uniform.

page.engineering_intro: The CJ-7 is old-school body-on-frame: a steel tub on six body mounts, leaf springs at all four corners, a part-time gear-driven transfer case (or the full-time, chain-drive Quadra-Trac option until 1979), a Dana 30 front axle with locking hubs, and AMC's Model 20 rear axle. Everything bolts together with hand tools, and almost every part is still made.

engineering.note: The rear section is stepped out to bring springs and shocks closer to the body. Check for cracks around the steering box.
Discs were optional in 1976 and standard from 1977. Six-bolt hubs to 1980, a weaker five-bolt Warn hub from 1981 to 1986.
Keyed two-piece hub-and-shaft design. Narrow track until 1981, wide track from 1982; some 1986 trucks got a Dana 44.
Low range is 2.03:1 in the Dana 20 and 2.62:1 in the Dana 300. Quadra-Trac (BW 13-39, full-time, chain) was optional from 1976 to 1979.
232: standard six 1976–78. 258: optional, then the base six from 1979; 110–115 hp from 1979, carbureted throughout. 304: until 1981. The four was standard from 1980.
The T-18A granny four-speed (1977–79) and the T-176 (1980–86) are the strong ones.

generations_table.note: T-150 or T-18/T-18A with Dana 20 (2.03:1 low), or TH400 with Quadra-Trac BW 13-39. The 258 became the base six for 1979.
Dana 300 arrives. SR-4, T-176 or TF999 auto. Last year of the 304 is 1981.
Axles 4 inches wider. T-4, T-5, T-176, TF999 or TF904 auto. The 258 is the only six.
2,500 built. In 1982 there was also the Jamboree, 630 numbered trucks marking the Rubicon Trail's 30th anniversary.
Built in Ohio for export only. T-176, Dana 300, 4.10 gears.
AMC 20 supply ran out and some trucks got a wide-track, 30-spline Dana 44 rear with flanged one-piece shafts (Offroaders.com puts the change between serials ending 049379 and 054173).

buying_checks.head: Frame first, everything else second
buying_checks.body: JeepCJ.com's buyer's guide starts with the frame. Probe the front and rear spring-shackle mounts, where mud blocks the drain holes in the boxed rails, the area behind the rear wheels, and all six body mounts. The guide says to check them with a hammer and screwdriver.

buying_checks.head: Look for cracks around the steering box
buying_checks.body: The guide says the area around the steering box is one of the most common places for a CJ frame to crack, especially on lifted trucks or trucks on big tires. Look for fresh paint, weld beads or splice plates and ask what was done.

buying_checks.head: Tub, floors and windshield frame
buying_checks.body: Check the rockers, rear corners, wheel wells, the area under the roll bar and the floor; lift any carpet. The bottom of the windshield frame and its hinges rust, often from a leaking defroster. On 1982–86 wide-track trucks, check the front-fender shock towers, which trap water.

buying_checks.head: Know which gearbox you're buying
buying_checks.body: A T-18A (1977–79) or T-176 (1980–86) is what you want. The SR-4, T-4 and T-5 are light-duty Borg-Warner boxes that Novak says suffer from sheared splines and stretched cases behind the 258. Check the casting number on the driver's side: 13-32 or 13-40 for an SR-4, 13-51 for a T-4, 13-52 for a T-5.

buying_checks.head: Inspect the AMC 20's two-piece shafts
buying_checks.body: On a stock CJ rear axle the hub is keyed onto the shaft and held with a big nut. If the nut loosens, the key shears and that wheel stops driving. Look for one-piece axle shafts in the receipts, or budget for them. Read the gear-code stamp on the housing to the left of the cover.

buying_checks.head: Quadra-Trac trucks need a test
buying_checks.body: On gravel, try high and (if fitted) low range and listen for chain noise. The JeepCJ.com guide says the chain stretches, possibly to the point of jumping teeth, if the oil level wasn't kept up. Quadra-Trac trucks have drive plates instead of locking hubs, and the vacuum 'Emergency Drive' control locks the center differential; check that it engages.

buying_checks.head: Listen to the carburetor
buying_checks.body: Stumbling and stalling at idle usually means a Carter BBD with clogged idle tubes, and its tangle of emissions vacuum hoses is the other usual suspect. Not a deal-breaker, but price in a clean-up or a Weber or EFI swap.

buying_checks.head: Electrics and emissions bits
buying_checks.body: Duct-tape splices, wire nuts, Scotch-locks and foil-wrapped fuses are warning signs, and most CJ electrical faults come down to rusty grounds. If your state inspects 1980s trucks, check that the TAC air cleaner, EGR, PCV and air-pump hardware are still there; the guide notes air-pump pulleys and brackets are hard to find.

repairs.title: Convert the AMC 20 to one-piece axle shafts
repairs.time: ≈ A day, plus tube welding if you do it
repairs.symptoms: A clunk under load, a rear wheel that suddenly stops driving, or a hub that wobbles on its shaft. The key between the shaft and the pressed-on hub shears once the big hub nut loosens. Or you've simply bought a CJ with original two-piece shafts and bigger tires.
repairs.fix: Pull the drums, the hub nut and the hub (this needs a proper hub puller), then the backing-plate bolts, and pull the old shafts. Buy the kit for your axle: narrow track for 1976–81, wide track for 1982–86. Install the new one-piece shafts with the bearings and seals supplied (some kits need a special bearing), set the end play, and refit the brakes. While the axle is apart, JeepCJ.com members suggest stitch-welding the tubes to the center section, using three 1 to 1.5-inch welds rather than a continuous bead, to stop the thin tubes from twisting.
repairs.tools: Hub puller · slide hammer · 1/2 in breaker bar · dial indicator for end play · welder (optional) · 80W-90 gear oil.

parts.name: Crown RT23007 AMC 20 one-piece axle shaft kit (76–83 CJ-5, 76–81 CJ-7, narrow track)
Crown RT23008 AMC 20 one-piece axle shaft kit (82–86 CJ, wide track)
Omix 16536.07 AMC 20 one-piece axle bearing & hardware kit (76–86 CJ)
Omix 16534.03 outer axle seal, AMC 20 one-piece axles

repairs.title: Repair a cracked frame at the steering box
repairs.time: ≈ A weekend, or a day at a weld shop
repairs.cost: Steel and welding wire; several members recommend paying a weld shop
repairs.symptoms: Steering that wanders or clunks, a steering box that moves when someone turns the wheel with the engine running, or a visible crack in the driver's frame rail near the box. Lifted trucks and trucks on big tires crack more often.
repairs.fix: Find the end of the crack and drill a small hole there to stop it spreading. Remove the box, clean the rail to bare metal and weld the crack. Then add splice plates: one owner cut 1/8-inch plate long enough to extend a few inches past the crack on each side. One member's advice is to weld the top and bottom in intermittent beads (about 1 inch of weld, 2 inches of gap) and leave the plate ends unwelded, because welds concentrate stress. Several owners say their DIY MIG repairs failed next to the welds and a weld shop's held. Add a steering-box brace to tie the box to the opposite rail, and replace any rotted frame sections with weld-in repair pieces.
repairs.tools: Drill and bits · angle grinder · welder (or a shop) · 1/8 in steel plate · clamps · torch for normalizing (optional).

parts.name: Rust Buster front center frame section, 76–86 CJ-5/CJ-7/CJ-8 (weld-in, 11 ga)
Crown J5363231 power steering box, 80–86 CJ (if the box is worn out too)
Steering box brace, CJ-7 (search)

repairs.title: Clean the Carter BBD idle tubes
repairs.cost: A can of carb cleaner and a pair of venturi gaskets
repairs.symptoms: Stumbling and sputtering at idle, stalling at stop signs, poor fuel economy, or an idle that someone has turned up to hide the problem. Offroaders.com says the most common cause is clogged idle tubes letting fuel drip from the venturis, so it runs rich.
repairs.fix: With the engine idling and the choke open, look down the carb: fuel dripping from the venturi nozzles at idle means the idle tubes are clogged. Engine off. Remove the air cleaner (tag the hoses), the choke-plate screws, the choke-rod clip and screw, then the two screws holding the venturi cluster, and lift it out with its two gaskets. Spray everything with carb cleaner without dislodging the center check ball, clear the idle tubes and nozzles with fine wire, and reassemble with every body screw tight. The article says Jeep once recommended drilling the idle tubes to 0.032 in to stop them clogging again. If it still idles badly, look for split vacuum hoses and intake leaks before blaming the carb.
repairs.tools: Screwdrivers · snap-ring pliers · carb cleaner · fine wire · masking tape for labeling hoses.

parts.name: Carter BBD rebuild kit & gaskets, 1983 CJ-7 4.2L
Weber K551-38-S 38-DGES carburetor kit, 72–90 CJ/YJ 4.2L (replacement option)
Holley 550-858K Sniper EFI BBD master kit, 71–86 CJ 258 (EFI option)

repairs.title: Replace rotten floor pans and body mounts
repairs.time: ≈ A weekend or more per side
repairs.cost: Panels are cheap; the labor is in the cutting and welding
repairs.symptoms: Daylight through the floor, wet carpet, a tub that shifts on the frame, or body mounts you can push a screwdriver through. The buyer's guide points to the floor, rockers, rear corners and the area under the roll bar.
repairs.fix: Strip the interior and lift the carpet. Cut back to solid metal, then trim the replacement pan to overlap or butt-fit, and plug-weld it along the factory seams. Seam-seal and paint the inside and out. Replace the rubber body-mount bushings at the same time: loosen all six mount bolts, jack the tub a little at each mount, and swap the upper and lower bushings. If a frame-side mount bracket has rotted, weld in a new one before refitting the tub.
repairs.tools: Cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · MIG welder · panel clamps · seam sealer · weld-through primer · floor jack and wood block.

parts.name: Key Parts 0479-221 front floor pan, 76–86 CJ-7/CJ-8
Key Parts 1/2 floor pan, 76–95 CJ-7/CJ-8/YJ
Crown J5462447 upper body mount bushing, 76–86 CJ-5/CJ-7/CJ-8
Rust Buster RB1007 body-to-frame mount, 76–86 CJ-7 (weld-in)

repairs.title: Rebuild rusted rear shackle mounts and replace shackles and bushings
repairs.cost: Repair sections and shackles are under a few hundred dollars
repairs.symptoms: A rear end that sits crooked or crashes over bumps, squeaking leaf springs, or a shackle hanger with rust holes. The buyer's guide calls the shackle mounts a common rot spot, because mud blocks the boxed frame's drain holes.
repairs.fix: Support the frame on stands and take the weight off the springs. Unbolt the shackle and spring eye, and cut out the rotted hanger section. Weld in a slip-fit repair section, then paint and wax-oil the inside of the rail. Fit new shackles (greaseable ones let you lube the pivots) and new bushings in the spring eyes and frame mounts. Torque the bolts with the truck at ride height so the bushings aren't preloaded twisted.
repairs.tools: Jack stands · cut-off wheel · welder · grease gun · bushing press or vise.

parts.name: Rust Buster rear shackle mount section, 76–86 CJ-5/CJ-7
Fishbone Offroad 1/2 in greaseable shackles, 76–86 CJ-7
Energy Suspension Hyper-Flex complete bushing kit, 80–86 CJ-5/CJ-7

repairs.title: Service the front wheel bearings and locking hubs
repairs.cost: Bearings, races and seals [price not sourced]
repairs.symptoms: Play at the top and bottom of the tire, growling that changes when you turn, grease flung inside the rim, or hubs that won't engage. The stock five-bolt Warn hubs on 1981–86 CJs are weak, and Quadra-Trac trucks have drive plates rather than hubs.
repairs.fix: Remove the hub, the outer nut, lock washer and inner nut, then pull the rotor and catch the outer bearing. Clean everything, replace bearings and races as pairs, and press the new races in square. Seals come in two sizes (2 1/8 in and 2 5/16 in), so measure the old one first. Pack the bearings fully and tighten the inner nut to 50 ft-lb while turning the rotor to seat them, as the manuals quoted in the Off-Road.com thread say. Then back it off (one owner backs off about 1/6 turn), fit the lock washer and torque the outer locknut to 50 ft-lb and bend the lock-washer lip over it (1981 Jeep factory service manual; the inner nut is set the same way there, 50 ft-lb then back off 1/6 turn), and check end play: the manuals quoted there specify 0.001–0.005 in with a dial indicator. If the six spindle bolts come out, replace the needle bearing inside the spindle too.
repairs.tools: Hub/spindle-nut socket · torque wrench · bearing packer (optional) · race driver or long bolt · brake cleaner · high-quality wheel-bearing grease.

parts.name: Crown SET45 front outer wheel bearing kit, 76–86 CJ
Crown SET47 front inner wheel bearing set, 77–86 CJ
Yukon AK F-J01 front axle bearing & seal kit, 76–83 CJ-5/CJ-7 Dana 30
Mile Marker 470 stainless manual locking hubs, 81–86 CJ (5-bolt)

repairs.title: Reseal a leaking Dana 300
repairs.cost: A seal kit and 2 quarts of 80W-90
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the skid plate, wet yokes or a drip from the rear output. The Dana 300 holds only 2 quarts, so a slow leak can starve it.
repairs.fix: Drain the case and unbolt the driveshafts. Hold the yoke and remove the output nut, then pull the yoke. Pry the old seal out with a big screwdriver or small pry bar, and drive the new one in squarely with a seal driver or a large socket (one owner used a 1 1/2-inch socket), tapping gently so it doesn't distort. Inspect the yoke's seal surface and replace it if it's grooved. Many owners take the chance to switch from strap-style to U-bolt yokes. Refill with 80W-90 to the fill plug.
repairs.tools: Yoke holder or pipe wrench · large socket for the output nut · pry bar · seal driver or 1 1/2 in socket · 80W-90 gear oil.

parts.name: Crown 300GK Dana 300 transfer case seal kit, 80–86 CJ
Crown Dana 300 rear output shaft inner bearing, CJ
Yukon 80W90 conventional gear oil

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: A 31x10.50R15 on the right wheel, on a healthy stock CJ-7. Performance Plus Tire's guide says it needs healthy springs and shallow backspacing (about 3.5 in on a 15x8 for narrow-track trucks), and JeepCJ.com owners agree 31s are the practical limit. One member reported 32x11.50s on a stock CJ with very little rubbing. 33x12.50R15s need a lift; most CJs running 33s have about 4 inches of spring lift, though 2.5 inches can work with the right backspacing and some fender trimming. Every CJ-7 used 15-inch wheels on a 5 x 5.5 in bolt pattern, with factory sizes from H78-15 bias-plies to metric radials up to 235/75R15 (Performance Plus).

faq.q: Should I keep the AMC 20 or swap it?
faq.a: The AMC 20 has a bigger ring gear (8⅞ in) than a Dana 44, but thinner 29-spline shafts, smaller tubes and, on CJs, keyed two-piece hub-and-shaft axles that shear. On a mild truck, one-piece shafts and stitch-welded tubes fix most of it. If you're running big tires and a locker, the usual swap is a Dana 44, and some late-1986 CJ-7s came with a wide-track Dana 44 from the factory.

faq.q: Which transmission should I look for?
faq.a: The T-18A (1977–79) with its 6.32:1 granny first is the toughest factory CJ gearbox. From 1980, the Tremec T-176 four-speed (3.52:1 first) is the strong option. The SR-4 (1980–81) and the T-4 and T-5 (1982–86) are light-duty Borg-Warner boxes that Novak calls 'essentially a small car transmission in a truck'.

The Dana 300 (1980–86) has a 2.62:1 low range against the Dana 20's 2.03:1, and helical low-range gears that make it quieter. Novak says there's probably no real strength advantage, and the Dana 20 is shorter, which helps driveshaft angles. For more crawl, TeraFlex's TeraLow gearset gives a Dana 300 a 4:1 low range; one owner's crawl ratio went from 32.3:1 to 49.8:1.

faq.q: What is Quadra-Trac, and should I keep it?
faq.a: Quadra-Trac was the optional full-time 4WD in 1976–79 CJ-7s: a chain-driven Borg-Warner 13-39 case paired only with a TH400 automatic. It has a vacuum-locked center differential (the 'Emergency Drive' switch) and an optional bolt-on low range (2.57:1). The chain is known for a short life. Mile Marker sold an overdrive gear-and-chain set that also converts it to part-time, and Offroaders.com names the Dana 18 as a good gear-driven replacement because its outputs line up (it needs a transmission swap too).

faq.q: How do I find my axle ratio?
faq.a: Look for the code stamped on the AMC 20 housing boss to the left of the cover, near the tube. Narrow-track codes differ from wide-track ones: on a wide-track axle, A is 3.54 open, AA is 3.54 Trac-Lok, H is 3.73 open, and C is 4.10 open. Offroaders.com advises confirming with a tape measure or the front axle's Dana tag, because codes conflict between versions. Offroaders.com gives the common Dana 30 ratios as 3.54 for 1976–79 and 2.73 for 1980–86, while Wikipedia pairs the 258 and four with 3.73 and the 304 with 3.55, so check yours rather than assume.

faq.q: What's the difference between narrow track and wide track?
faq.a: 1976–81 CJ-7s use narrow-track axles, 50.5 in wheel to wheel on the AMC 20. From 1982 the wide-track axles measure 54.5 in, which helps stability. Both use 5 x 5.5 in wheels. The 1982–86 Dana 30 also switched to pin-bolted calipers and crimped brake hoses.

faq.q: Which engine is the one to have?
faq.a: The 258 straight six (1976–78 trucks may have the smaller 232 six, which was standard until 1979). JeepCJ.com's buyer's guide calls it 'a strong, torquey, reliable motor' and says to avoid the GM Iron Duke four (1980–83). The 304 V8 (to 1981) is quicker but was choked by smog controls by the end: 125 hp in 1980–81 against the 258's 110.

ExtremeTerrain's CJ guide lists 80W-90 gear oil for the Dana 30 (1.25 qt), AMC 20 (2.4 qt; add 4 oz of limited-slip additive for Trac-Lok), Dana 300 (2 qt) and Dana 20 (1.6 qt). Quadra-Trac needs its own transfer case fluid (2.25 qt). The T-176, SR-4, T-150 and T-18 take 80W-90; ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4 for the T-4 and T-5 and for the automatics, while the 1981 Jeep factory manual calls for Dexron or Dexron II in the 999 and 904 automatics and SAE 85W-90 GL-5 in the axles, the manual gearboxes and the Dana 300. The T-4/T-5 and the TH400 (a GM unit) aren't covered there, so check your manual before filling them [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. Brakes take DOT 3. The 258 takes about 6 quarts of oil including the filter, per ExtremeTerrain and a 1984 owner's manual quoted on JeepCJ.com, and about 10.5 qt of coolant (ExtremeTerrain).

faq.q: Will Wrangler wheels and parts fit?
faq.a: Not the wheels. CJ axles use 5 x 5.5 in, and later Jeep Dana 30s use 5 x 4.5 in. Lots of other parts carry over, though: the 258 lived on in the YJ until 1990, and outer Dana 30 parts (knuckle outward) swap between CJ versions, so a drum-brake CJ can be converted to discs.
Only for export. From 1980 to 1982 AMC built CJ-7s in Ohio with Isuzu's 2.4-liter C240 diesel four, a T-176, a Dana 300 and 4.10 axles. None were sold new in the US.

mods.why: Old CJ leaf springs sag and ride like a cart. New springs, shackles and bushings cure it. A popular upgrade is to fit hangers that let you run Wrangler YJ leaf springs.

mods.why: The factory bumpers are thin. A steel front bumper gives you a winch mount and recovery points, and a rear tube bumper with D-rings protects the tub corners, which tend to rust anyway.
Put one-piece shafts in the AMC 20 before you add a locker, or the locker will find the weak keyed hubs quickly.

mods.why: The Dana 300 takes a 4:1 low-range gearset, its shifter interlock can be removed for twin-stick operation, and Novak and Advance Adapters can help you swap out a weak T-4 or T-5.
The computer-controlled BBD is the 258's weakest link. A Weber 38 kit or Holley's bolt-on Sniper EFI replaces it.

mods.why: A new soft top keeps you drier. Officially licensed replacement panels mean even a rotten tub can be saved.

baseline_service.intro: Assume a 40-year-old CJ-7 has had nothing done unless there are receipts, and remember that three owners ago someone probably swapped the gearbox, carb or axle. Identify what you actually have first (Dana 20, Dana 300 or Quadra-Trac; which transmission; narrow or wide track), because the fluids differ. Then change every fluid, repack the front bearings and grease every zerk.

items.spec: About 6 qt including the filter, per a 1984 CJ-7 owner's manual quoted on JeepCJ.com · ExtremeTerrain lists 5W-30 or 10W-30 for CJ engines
items.interval: Then every 7,500 mi or 7.5 months after a first change at 5,000 (1981 Jeep factory schedule). Many owners use 3,000–5,000 mi on an old carbureted six
items.note: Owners report 5 to 5.5 qt reaching FULL depending on the pan and filter, so fill to 5, run it, then top up on the dipstick. The 304 V8 takes 5 qt and the 2.5 four takes 4 qt (ExtremeTerrain). The MFK16 and MFK18 kits below are for 304 and 2.5L trucks, not the 258.
